paper_title: Seasonality in the Cross-Section of Stock Returns†
summary: Deprioritize. The paper by Heston and Sadka reports that stocks which did well in the same calendar month in earlier years tend to do well in that month again, and the tested version sorts stocks into deciles on average returns at annual lags 24, 36, 48, and 60 months. Our long-only, equal-weighted test on a 415-name survivor universe over 2015 to 2025 returned a net CAGR of 8.03% against 12.71% for the equal-weighted universe, with a Sharpe of 0.38 against 0.65. The Monte Carlo fund economics are also negative: the probability that the net present value is positive is 12%, and the median incremental fee present value is -$3.0M against the equal-weighted universe fund. The main reason for the recommendation is that the strategy trails its benchmark, the edge fails at 10 bps of costs, and the decile ranking runs opposite to the paper's expected direction.
